text:
Ana Morales: quick sync — SDR heatmap for competitor claims is ready, want to finalize 3 variants for trial handout by EOD
Mike Chen: nice. can you paste the heatmap?
Ana Morales: https://internal.redwood/heatmaps/sdr-claims-1799 :eyes:
Priya Patel: reading it now. top friction: 'we already use cloud AI' and 'why not call the model directly'
Tom Rivera: For cloud AI angle, can we lean on cost + predictable latency? short line: "Predictable latency and controllable unit economics — not just model access."
Sasha Li: For infra vendors, push the ops burden point: "We manage inference economics while you build features. No infra lift."
Mike Chen: love those. can we draft 3 one-liners per competitor segment? i.e. Cloud APIs / LLM-as-a-service / Self-host infra
Ana Morales: sure — first pass: 
- Cloud APIs: "Consistent production performance across regions and SLAs — more than an API key."
- LLM APIs: "Streaming, function calling, and model rollouts with observability built-in."
- Infra vendors: "Turnkey inference runtime + ops playbook — avoid hiring bespoke SREs."
Priya Patel: shorter versions for SDR scripts: 
`Cloud: predictable latency, predictable cost.`
`LLM API: full production features, not just sampling.`
`Infra: zero infra lift, standard SLAs.`
Tom Rivera: add a quick benchmark note we can cite: 
ProductBot: benchmark update: hosted median p95 latency (gen-16k tokens) = 220ms; competitor A = 480ms; competitor B = 310ms. metrics spreadsheet: https://internal.redwood/reports/bench-march-1799
Sasha Li: can we avoid naming competitors in the SDR script, use contrast language? e.g. "vs generic cloud endpoints"
Mike Chen: yes. also need objection responses: short Q/A pair for each claim
Ana Morales: draft objections: 
- Q: "Why not just use cloud provider?" A: "Cloud provider endpoints vary by region and topology — Redwood offers SLA-backed latency and predictable unit economics you can plan for."
- Q: "Why not use direct model API?" A: "Model access is table stakes; Redwood adds production controls — rollouts, fallback routing, cost controls."
- Q: "Is this more ops?" A: "No — Dedicated and Private options designed to remove infra lift; we take over inference ops and observability."
Priya Patel: love. can marketing ops make a 1-page heatmap + a 2-column battlecard for SDRs?
Mike Chen: i'll own the battlecard layout. Ana — can you confirm final one-liners by 4pm?
Ana Morales: yep will push updates by 3:45pm.
Sasha Li: i'll pair with Mike on the 2-column format, will add quick rebut bullets. :thumbsup:
Tom Rivera: put the benchmark callouts in bold on top and link to the spreadsheet.
ProductBot: reminder: webinar slot reserved May 12, 10am PT — "Benchmarking Inference: routing & economics". RSVP: https://internal.redwood/events/webinar-1799
Ana Morales: perfect — we'll use the heatmap and battlecard as pre-webinar assets. thanks team.
Mike Chen: thanks all. will update thread with the first draft.
